# has tag

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:hasTag`](gmeow-hasTag.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTag>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/tags`](../../slices/tags.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

Relates an entity to a user-minted tag — the 80% flat shortcut. Non-functional: an entity may carry many co-equal tags. Period, confidence, tagger and suppression are carried via RDF-star statement annotations ([`gmeow:validFrom`](gmeow-validFrom.md), [`gmeow:validUntil`](gmeow-validUntil.md), [`gmeow:confidence`](gmeow-confidence.md), [`gmeow:displayable`](gmeow-displayable.md)) on the shortcut; promote to a [`gmeow:Tagging`](../classes/gmeow-Tagging.md) relator when the act itself must be a node.

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:Entity`](../classes/gmeow-Entity.md) -> [`gmeow:Tag`](../classes/gmeow-Tag.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:hasTag`](gmeow-hasTag.md) from [`gmeow:Entity`](../classes/gmeow-Entity.md) to [`gmeow:Tag`](../classes/gmeow-Tag.md) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

### Folksonomy

- **Source:** [`slices/core/tags/examples/folksonomy.ttl`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/slices/core/tags/examples/folksonomy.ttl)
- **Examples catalog:** [open in catalog](../../examples/index.md#example-slices-core-tags-examples-folksonomy)#example-slices-core-tags-examples-folksonomy

```turtle
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Blackcat Informatics® Inc. <paudley@blackcatinformatics.ca>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0
#
# Worked example: tagging is flat-first, reified on demand ( P4). A bare
# gmeow:hasTag covers "this is tagged X". Tags themselves form a SKOS-style poly-
# hierarchy (gmeow:broaderTag / gmeow:narrowerTag / gmeow:relatedTag) inside a
# gmeow:TagScheme. When the PROVENANCE of a tagging matters — who applied it, in
# which scheme — it is promoted to a reified gmeow:Tagging relator binding tagger
# × tagged × tag × scheme, so a contested or machine-applied tag is auditable.
@prefix gmeow: <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/> .
@prefix ex:    <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/examples/tags/> .
@prefix rdfs:  <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .

# --- Flat tagging: the common case.
ex:paper a gmeow:CreativeWork ;
    gmeow:title  "A Survey of Transformer Architectures"@en ;
    gmeow:hasTag ex:tagML .
```

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use as the default, flat way to attach an informal label to any entity; carry period, confidence, tagger, or suppression as RDF-star annotations on the statement when the simple metadata is enough.

### Avoid when

- Avoid when the act of tagging must be a first-class node with full provenance (promote to [`gmeow:Tagging`](../classes/gmeow-Tagging.md)) and avoid using it for subject-matter ([`gmeow:isAbout`](gmeow-isAbout.md)) or classification ([rdf:type](http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type)); the three axes are disjoint.

### How to use

- Assert ex:entity [`gmeow:hasTag`](gmeow-hasTag.md) ex:tag; annotate the statement with gmeow:validFrom/validUntil, [`gmeow:confidence`](gmeow-confidence.md), or [`gmeow:displayable`](gmeow-displayable.md) for lightweight metadata, and reify to [`gmeow:Tagging`](../classes/gmeow-Tagging.md) (which it [`pairsWith`](gmeow-pairsWith.md)) when those must be queryable nodes.

### Examples
